name: ios
description: Build, test, sign and ship native iOS apps from a machine without Xcode, by driving a Mac over SSH: new projects, tap-to-install builds on your phone, and App Store listings with a tapped submission.

setup.prompt: The Mac that builds, as you would ssh to it (key auth, Xcode installed)
A second Mac to use when the first is unreachable
Your Apple developer Team ID (developer.apple.com > Membership)
Your distribution signing identity, for App Store builds
Prefix for new apps' bundle ids
The https address that serves your install pages (iOS requires HTTPS)
Folder the install pages are written to
Where Node lives, if it is not on PATH

steps: Make the build Mac reachable over SSH with key auth, with release Xcode installed and signed in to your Apple developer account.
On the Mac, in a GUI Terminal once, create a build keychain holding your Apple signing identities and save its password to ~/.config/build-keychain-pw (README.md explains why).

Create an App Store Connect API key (Users and Access > Integrations), copy the .p8 to ~/private_keys/ on the Mac, and store its key_id, issuer_id and key_path with herald secret request appstore.key_id and friends.
Serve ios.ota_dir over HTTPS at ios.ota_url, for example with a static server and tailscale serve.
